extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Singular computer algebra system (researchers/practitioners in computational algebra, D-module theory, and noncommutative/letterplace Groebner basis computations)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for Singular library procedures (dmodvar.lib and fpadim.lib) describing usage, inputs, outputs, assumptions, and optional parameters for D-module and Letterplace/finite-presented algebra computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: isInt
rubrics_metrics.description: isInt(n); n a number — Return: int, 1 if n is an integer or 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: check whether given object of type number is actually an int. Note: Parameters are treated as integers. Example: number n = 4/3; isInt(n) -> 0. n = 11; isInt(n) -> 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: sortIntvec
rubrics_metrics.description: sortIntvec(v); v an intvec — Return: list of two intvecs. Purpose: sorts an intvec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the output list L, the first entry consists of the entries of v satisfying L[1][i] >= L[1][i+1]. The second entry is a permutation such that v[L[2]] = L[1]. Unlike in the procedure sort, zeros are not dismissed. Examples show negative and zero entries preserved. See also sort (Section D.2.3.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: dmodvar.lib overview (data of interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of algebraic D-module computations for varieties: given R=K[x1..xn] and F=f1*...*fr, study R[1/F]*F^s as a D<S>-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data of interest listed by the library: the left ideal Ann F^s in D<S> (output LD); the global Bernstein polynomial bs (in variable s=s1+...+sr); its minimal integer root s0 and the list BS of all roots with multiplicities; an r-tuple of operators PS such that sum_k P_k * f_k * F^s = bs * F^s in R[1/F]*F^s. References: BMS06, ALM09. Cross-references to related libraries (bfun, dmod, dmodapp, gmssing).

rubrics_metrics.name: bfctVarIn
rubrics_metrics.description: bfctVarIn(I [,a,b,c]); I an ideal, a,b,c optional ints — Return: list of ideal and intvec. Purpose: computes roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial and multiplicities for an affine variety defined by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is commutative over field char 0 and variable names don't include t(1..r) or Dt(1..r) where r=#entries of I. Output L: L[1] (ideal) contains rational roots of b-function; L[2] (intvec) contains multiplicities; optional L[3] (string) is part of b-function without rational roots. Encoding notes: degree 0 b-function encoded via L[1][1]=0, L[2]=0 and L[3]=1 or 0. Flags: if a<>0 use ideal as given otherwise use a heuristically better generating set; if b<>0 use std for GB otherwise slimgb; if c<>0 use matrix ordering otherwise block ordering. Implementation note: computes initial ideal of multivariate Malgrange ideal then solves linear system by linear reductions (following Noro). Result is shifted by 1 - codim(Var(F)) per BMS06. Display: printlevel controls debug/progress messages. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: bfctVarAnn
rubrics_metrics.description: bfctVarAnn(F[,gid,eng]); F an ideal, gid,eng optional ints — Return: list of an ideal and an intvec. Purpose: computes roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial and multiplicities for an affine variety defined by F=F[1..F[r]].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering commutative over field char 0. Output: ideal contains all roots and intvec their multiplicities. Flags: gid<>0 use ideal as given otherwise heuristic generator selection; eng<>0 use std for Groebner basis computations otherwise slimgb. Computational remark: runtime may vary greatly depending on chosen generators though result is same. Implementation: computes annihilator of f^s in D[s] then solves linear system by linear reductions to find minimal polynomial of S = sum s(i)(i). Result is shifted by 1 - codim(Var(F)) following BMS06. Display: printlevel controls debug messaging. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: SannfsVar
rubrics_metrics.description: SannfsVar(F [,ORD,eng]); F an ideal, ORD an optional string, eng an optional int — Return: ring (Weyl algebra tensored with U(gl P)) containing an ideal LD. Purpose: compute the D<S>-module structure of D<S>*f^s according to algorithm by Briancon and Maisonobe for affine varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering commutative over field char 0. Activate the output ring with setring to inspect result; ideal LD is the D<S>-module structure. ORD must be an elimination ordering in D<Dt,S> for Dt written in string form, otherwise result may have no meaning; default ORD='(a(1..(P)..1),a(1..(P+P^2)..1),dp)'. If eng<>0 use std for Groebner basis computations otherwise slimgb. Display controlled by printlevel. Example demonstrates output ring, noncommutative relations, and LD generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeMalgrange
rubrics_metrics.description: makeMalgrange(F [,ORD]); F an ideal, ORD an optional string — Return: ring (Weyl algebra) containing an ideal IF. Purpose: create the Malgrange ideal associated with F=F[1..P].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activate output ring with setring to examine IF (the Malgrange ideal). ORD must be an arbitrary ordering in K< t, x, Dt, Dx> written as a string; default ORD='dp'. Display: printlevel controls progress/debug messages. Example shows resulting IF and relations (Dt(i) t(i) = t(i) Dt(i)+1 etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: fpadim.lib overview (letterplace finite-presented algebra tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview: given free associative algebra A=K<x1..xn> and a finite Groebner basis GB, compute K-dimension and explicit K-basis of A/<GB>, Ufnarovskij graph, mistletoes, and Hilbert series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key concepts: Ufnarovskij graph used to detect finiteness (check cycles); basis tree and mistletoes (endpoints) determine K-basis. Uses Letterplace format: monomials represented as intvecs (variable numbers). Notes: basering is always a Letterplace ring; all intvecs correspond to Letterplace monomials; if specifying degree bound d, require d <= attrib(basering,uptodeg). Cross-reference freegb.lib. References given (Ufnarovskij, Levandovskyy/La Scala, Studzinski).

rubrics_metrics.name: lpMis2Dim
rubrics_metrics.description: lpMis2Dim(M); M an ideal — Return: int, the K-dimension of the factor algebra. Purpose: computing K-dimension from given mistletoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and M contains only monomials. Note: mistletoes must be ordered lexicographically (OrdMisLex). Example shows usage with a Letterplace ring and returns integer dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpKDim
rubrics_metrics.description: lpKDim(G[,degbound,n]); G an ideal, degbound and n optional integers — Return: int, the K-dimension of the factor algebra. Purpose: computing K-dimension of a factor algebra given via an ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. degbound (if set) must satisfy degbound <= attrib(basering,uptodeg). degbound=0 means no degree bound; default attrib(basering,uptodeg). n is number of variables, default attrib(basering,lV). If K-dimension known infinite, a degree bound is needed. Examples show invocation with and without degree bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpDimCheck
rubrics_metrics.description: lpDimCheck(G) — Return: int, 1 if K-dimension of the factor algebra is infinite, 0 otherwise. Purpose: checking factor algebra for finiteness of K-dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. Examples demonstrate return 0 for finite and 1 for infinite K-dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpMis2Base
rubrics_metrics.description: lpMis2Base(M); M an ideal — Return: ideal, a K-basis of the factor algebra. Purpose: computing a K-basis from given mistletoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and M contains only monomials. Note: mistletoes must be ordered lexicographically (OrdMisLex). Example returns basis elements in ring notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpHilbert
rubrics_metrics.description: lpHilbert(G[,degbound,n]); G an ideal, degbound and n optional integers — Return: intvec containing coefficients of the Hilbert series. Purpose: computing the Hilbert series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. degbound (if set) must satisfy degbound <= attrib(basering,uptodeg). degbound=0 means no degree bound. n is number of variables (default attrib(basering,lV)). If I is returned then I[k] is the (k-1)-th coefficient of Hilbert series. If K-dimension is infinite, degree bound required. Examples provided, and note that optional params often unnecessary when K-dimension is finite.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpDHilbert
rubrics_metrics.description: lpDHilbert(G[,degbound,n]); G an ideal, degbound and n optional integers — Return: list. Purpose: compute K-dimension and Hilbert series starting with a Letterplace ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If L is returned then L[1] is integer dimension and L[2] is intvec of Hilbert coefficients. degbound and n behave as in lpHilbert. If K-dimension infinite, degree bound needed. Examples show list structure and invocation variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpDHilbertSickle
rubrics_metrics.description: lpDHilbertSickle(G[,degbound,n]); G an ideal, degbound and n optional integers — Return: list. Purpose: compute K-dimension, Hilbert series and mistletoes at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. If L is returned then L[1] is integer K-dimension, L[2] is intvec Hilbert series, L[3] is ideal of mistletoes. degbound and n behave as in other lp* procedures. Examples demonstrate returned L[1..3].

rubrics_metrics.name: ivDHilbert
rubrics_metrics.description: ivDHilbert(L,n[,degbound]); L a list of intmats, n an integer, degbound optional — Return: list. Purpose: compute K-dimension and Hilbert series (input as intmats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and all rows of each intmat correspond to a Letterplace monomial. If L returned then L[1] is integer dimension and L[2] intvec of Hilbert coefficients. degbound optional (default none); if K-dimension infinite, degree bound needed. n is number of variables. Examples show outputs with and without degree bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivDHilbertSickle
rubrics_metrics.description: ivDHilbertSickle(L,n[,degbound]); L a list of intmats, n an integer, degbound optional — Return: list. Purpose: compute K-dimension, Hilbert series and mistletoes for intmat input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring; all rows of each intmat correspond to Letterplace monomials. Returned list L: L[1]=K-dimension (int), L[2]=intvec Hilbert series, L[3]=list of mistletoes as intvecs. degbound optional; n is number of variables. Examples show returned components and behavior with/without degree bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivDimCheck
rubrics_metrics.description: ivDimCheck(L,n); L a list of intmats, n an integer — Return: int, 0 if the dimension is finite, or 1 otherwise. Purpose: decide whether K-dimension is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring; all rows of each intmat correspond to letterplace monomials. n is number of variables. Examples illustrate return values for finite vs infinite factor algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivHilbert
rubrics_metrics.description: ivHilbert(L,n[,degbound]); L a list of intmats, n an integer, degbound optional — Return: intvec containing coefficients of the Hilbert series. Purpose: compute Hilbert series from intmat inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and all rows of each intmat correspond to Letterplace monomials. degbound optional (default none). If degbound set it must satisfy degbound <= attrib(basering,uptodeg). n is number of variables. If I returned then I[k] is (k-1)-th coefficient. If K-dimension infinite, degree bound needed. Examples show typical outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivKDim
rubrics_metrics.description: ivKDim(L,n[,degbound]); L a list of intmats, n an integer, degbound optional — Return: int, the K-dimension of A/<L>. Purpose: compute K-dimension of A/<L> from intmat representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and all rows of each intmat correspond to Letterplace monomials. degbound optional; if K-dimension known infinite, degree bound needed. n is number of variables. Examples show returned integer dimensions with and without degbound.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivMis2Base
rubrics_metrics.description: ivMis2Base(M); M a list of intvecs — Return: ideal, a K-base of the given algebra. Purpose: compute K-basis out of given mistletoes (intvec representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. Mistletoes must be ordered lexicographically -> OrdMisLex, otherwise some elements may be missing. Mistletoes stored as intvecs per overview. Example demonstrates mapping intvec mistletoes to basis output.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivMis2Dim
rubrics_metrics.description: ivMis2Dim(M); M a list of intvecs — Return: int, the K-dimension of the given algebra. Purpose: compute K-dimension from mistletoes in intvec form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. Mistletoes must be ordered lexicographically (OrdMisLex) otherwise returned value may differ. Example returns integer dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivOrdMisLex
rubrics_metrics.description: ivOrdMisLex(M); M a list of intvecs — Return: list containing the ordered intvecs of M. Purpose: orders a given set of mistletoes lexicographically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and intvecs correspond to monomials. This is preprocessing (not needed if mistletoes are returned from the sickle algorithm). Each entry of returned list is an intvec. Example shows lexicographic ordering effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivSickle
rubrics_metrics.description: ivSickle(L,n,[degbound]); L a list of intmats, n an int, degbound optional — Return: list containing intvecs, the mistletoes of A/<L>. Purpose: compute the mistletoes for a given Groebner basis L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and all rows of each intmat correspond to Letterplace monomials. If degbound specified, require degbound <= attrib(basering,uptodeg). degbound optional (0 means no degree bound by context). n is number of variables. If K-dimension infinite, degree bound is needed. Examples illustrate returned mistletoes and behaviour with/without degree bound.
